"The Sound of Silence," which was initially titled "The Sounds of Silence," is a song by the American music duo Simon & Garfunkel [1][3]. Paul Simon wrote the song over several months spanning 1963 and 1964 [1][3]. The recording for the song took place in March 1964 at Columbia Studios in New York City, intended for their debut album, *Wednesday Morning, 3 A.M.* [1][3].

The title of Simon & Garfunkel's second studio album was a minor alteration of the title of their initial major hit, "The Sound of Silence," which had originally been released as "The Sounds of Silence" [2][5]. An acoustic version of the song appeared on *Wednesday Morning, 3 A.M.* and later on the soundtrack for the film *The Graduate* [2]. Electric guitars, bass, and drums were added to the track by Columbia Records staff producer Tom Wilson without the knowledge of Paul Simon or Art Garfunkel [2]. Furthermore, electric overdubs for "The Sound of Silence" were recorded at Columbia's "Studio A" on June 15, 1965 [5].

Law enforcement agencies utilize specialized vehicles known as bait cars, which can also be called decoy cars, hot cars, or trap cars [1][3]. These cars are designed to capture thieves who steal items from automobiles or car thieves generally [1][3]. The vehicles are equipped with audio and video surveillance technology, allowing them to be remotely controlled and monitored [1][2][3].

When set up to catch thieves, these bait cars may include GPS tracking [1][3]. Furthermore, a "kill switch" might be installed, giving police the ability to remotely lock all doors or disable the engine to prevent escape [1][3]. For thefts involving items from cars, the vehicle can be disabled so that it cannot be started and will contain specially prepared "bait property" [2]. If the car is stolen, officers receive immediate alerts and can monitor the vehicle while sending commands such as locking doors, disabling the engine, or sounding the horn [2]. Additionally, bait cars can be part of a sting operation, where criminals are lured into exposing themselves [4].

*Jersey Shore* is an American reality television show that aired on MTV from December 3, 2009, until December 20, 2012 [1][2]. The program followed eight housemates who spent their summers together at a vacation home [1][2]. These locations varied across seasons: Seaside Heights, New Jersey, was used for seasons one, three, five, and six; South Beach, Florida, was the setting for season two; and Florence, Italy, hosted season four [1][2]. The series debuted amid controversy concerning its use of terms like "Guido/Guidette" and allegations regarding the perpetuation of stereotypes about Italian-Americans [1][2].

The Oriental Bank Corporation has a history dating back to the 19th century when it operated as a bank in India [4][5]. Specifically, it was established in Bombay, India, in 1842 under the name Bank of Western India [4][5]. Following the relocation of its headquarters to London in 1845, the name was changed to Oriental Bank Corporation [4][5]. The bank received a charter in 1851, which was intended to allow competition with the East India Company's opium billing monopoly, an activity that was unpopular in England at the time [4][5]. Furthermore, it holds the distinction of being the first bank in Hong Kong and the first bank there to issue banknotes [4][5].

The Rams played as the St. Louis Rams from 1995 through the 2015 seasons [2][3].

Windows Movie Maker was a video editing program from Microsoft [1][2]. It was initially included with Windows ME on September 14, 2000 [2]. The software was part of the Windows Essentials suite and allowed users to create and edit videos, as well as publish them to platforms like YouTube, Facebook, Vimeo, OneDrive, and Flickr [1][2].

Over time, the software evolved; for instance, a standalone product called Windows Live Movie Maker 2009 was released on August 19, 2009, which used a ribbon toolbar interface and could not read projects from older versions [4]. Later iterations included features like webcam capture and support for high-definition video with the release of Live Movie Maker 2011 [3]. However, the software was officially discontinued on January 10, 2017, and has since been replaced by "Windows Story Remix" built into Microsoft Photos in Windows 10 [1][2].
